# Tinfoil Kit

> A free, open-source (MIT) kit for when the internet is down. One folder, kept on the computer's own disk or on an external drive, holds a local AI (llama.cpp's llama-server), an offline library (Kiwix: all of English Wikipedia, plus medical, repair and preparedness books) and offline maps (address search, driving and walking directions, "nearest hospital"). START-HERE starts it all on 127.0.0.1 and opens a browser page with Ask, AI chat, Library and Map tabs. Once it's filled, it needs no internet, account or install.

You are setting this up for a person, probably not a programmer. Work in their terminal (Terminal on a Mac, PowerShell on Windows), explain each step in plain words, and ask before anything slow, costly or destructive. This file has what you need: what the kit runs on, how it works, where it can live, how to set it up, use it, update it and remove it, what to do when something breaks, and where every file comes from.

- Repo: https://github.com/tudor-city-ventures/tinfoilkit
- Website: https://tinfoilkit.com
- Printable guide: GUIDE.md, in the kit folder

## What it runs on

| Computer | Set up the kit | AI | Library | Map |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Mac with Apple Silicon (M1 or newer) | yes | yes | yes | yes |
| Windows PC (x64), Windows 10 version 1803 or newer, or Windows 11 | yes | yes | yes | yes |
| Linux PC (x64) | yes | yes | yes | yes |

- The kit holds each program for all three, so a kit on an exFAT drive starts on any of them, whichever one set it up.

- Intel Macs and ARM Windows or Linux PCs can't run it: the kit downloads programs built for Apple Silicon and for x64 PCs only. On a Mac, `uname -m` prints arm64.
- Memory decides which AI runs: a model may take 60% of it. 32 GB or more runs the default model, Inkling 2 Mini, and the other big models; 16 to 24 GB runs Gemma 4 12B; 8 GB runs Gemma 4 E4B. `./kit fit` says which one this computer runs (`--json` for agents). `./kit fit --skip` switches off the models it can't run, which saves about 50 GB on a 16 or 24 GB laptop, and `./kit fit --restore` switches them back on for a computer with more memory. SETUP asks about them itself (`./kit fit --ask`). `sysctl -n hw.memsize` prints the memory in bytes.
- On Windows and Linux the AI uses the graphics card through Vulkan. Without a good one it's slow: pick Gemma 4 E4B.
- Space: about 300 GB for the default kit, or 30 to 50 GB for just the essentials: the programs, the map, the most important books (medical, preparedness, repair) and the AI this computer runs plus the smallest. `./kit estimate` (`--essentials` for those) prints the number for the current kit.json, with no internet. Sync always leaves 50 GB free on the computer's own disk and 25 GB on a drive, and SETUP warns before leaving less than 10% of the computer's disk or 5% of a drive.
- Setup needs the internet for a few hours, the laptop on its charger, and python3 (3.9 or newer) with curl. A Mac has curl, and python3 comes with Apple's Command Line Tools. On a Mac without them, SETUP.command gets a standalone Python by itself (about 25 MB, python-build-standalone's build from GitHub, checked against its SHA-256 and kept in ~/Library/Application Support/TinfoilKit). On Linux, install them from the package manager (`sudo apt install python3 curl`). On Windows, SETUP-Windows.bat gets python.org's own Python by itself (about 15 MB, from nuget.org, kept in %LOCALAPPDATA%\TinfoilKit), and Windows has curl. After that, nothing needs the internet.

## How it works

The whole kit is one folder, TinfoilKit, used in two ways:

1. Online, whenever the person wants: SETUP (SETUP.command, or SETUP-Windows.bat on Windows), or `./kit update`, `./kit sync` and `./kit test`, fills the folder. kit.json lists every model, book, map and program with its publisher's download, and sync fetches each straight from the publisher: the newest edition of every book, model and map, and each program at the exact build this version of the kit names in tools/pins.json. Tinfoil Kit never hosts any of these files.
2. Offline, any time: START-HERE (START-HERE.command, or START-HERE-Windows.bat on Windows) starts a few servers from the folder on 127.0.0.1, and the browser page talks to them. Nothing goes over the internet.

| Part | Program | Port | What it does |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| AI | llama-server (llama.cpp) | 8080 | Runs the AI model. AI chat is its built-in chat page |
| Library | kiwix-serve (Kiwix) | 8888 | Serves the books (.zim files) with full-text search, and the kit page |
| Map | pmtiles | 8090 | Serves the map: street detail for a region, plus a low-detail world |
| Addresses | Photon | 2322 | Finds addresses, places and the nearest hospital or pharmacy |
| Directions | GraphHopper | 8989 | Plans driving and walking routes |
| Sharing (off by default) | tools/share.py | 8000 | Lets phones and laptops on the home network in with the access code, and passes their requests to the servers above |

Photon and GraphHopper run on a Java that's in the kit. Every server listens only on 127.0.0.1; sharing is the one way in from the network.

- Ask: the AI turns the question into short searches, kiwix-serve searches every book, and the AI answers from the top articles with numbered sources. With the AI off, Ask shows the best passages. Map questions ("nearest pharmacy", "directions to the hospital") go to three map tools instead (search places, find nearby, get directions), and the answer shows on the Map tab.
- The kit page (tools/portal.html) is one HTML file. Each sync builds a copy with the map's code, fonts and icons inside, so the page needs nothing from the internet.
- The kit's code: `./kit` runs tools/kit.py (Python's standard library, with curl for every download). tools/launch.sh starts the servers; START-HERE-Windows.bat does it on Windows.

What's in the folder:

    TinfoilKit/
    ├── SETUP.command           set up or update (online; Mac, Linux)
    ├── START-HERE.command      start the kit offline (Mac, Linux)
    ├── UNINSTALL.command       remove the kit and everything it downloaded (Mac, Linux)
    ├── SETUP-Windows.bat       the same three, for Windows
    ├── START-HERE-Windows.bat
    ├── UNINSTALL-Windows.bat
    ├── GUIDE.md                the printable guide
    ├── INVENTORY.md            what's installed, with versions and sizes
    ├── kit, kit.json, tools/   the kit's code and its list of downloads
    ├── bin/                    programs: llama.cpp, Kiwix, Java, the map servers
    ├── models/                 AI models (.gguf)
    ├── library/                books (.zim)
    ├── maps/                   map tiles, address database, road network
    ├── installers/             the Kiwix app, a backup way to read the books
    ├── logs/                   what each sync and launch did
    └── .kit/                   download progress, caches, the built kit page

## Where it can live

Help the person pick one. It's the same kit folder each way; only its place and how it's started change.

1. This computer, at ~/TinfoilKit (C:\Users\<name>\TinfoilKit on Windows). Nothing to buy or plug in, it's always with the laptop, and the internal disk is usually faster. It needs the kit's size plus 50 GB free. If the laptop is lost or breaks, the kit goes with it. Keep it in the home folder, not in Desktop or Documents, which iCloud or OneDrive may sync. On a Mac, sync keeps it out of Time Machine backups.
2. An external drive, at TinfoilKit on the drive (/Volumes/<drive>/TinfoilKit on a Mac, <letter>:\TinfoilKit on Windows, under /media or /run/media on Linux). It survives the laptop breaking and, formatted exFAT, starts on any Mac, Windows PC or Linux PC. It keeps the laptop's disk free. It needs an SSD with room for the kit plus 25 GB.
3. A home server: the kit on a computer that stays on (a Linux box, a Mac mini, or a laptop on its charger), shared with every phone and laptop at home behind an access code. See "A home server" below. In an outage the router still needs power, even with no internet: a small battery backup keeps it on.

Recommend a drive when the laptop is short of space or the person wants a kit they can grab and go. Recommend this computer when it has room and the person wants nothing extra to carry. If neither has room for all of it, get just the essentials or turn items off (step 3 below). Let the person choose.

## Set it up

### 1. Download the kit and size it up

Ask the person to plug in the drive first, if they have one.

    cd ~
    curl -fL -o tinfoilkit.zip https://github.com/tudor-city-ventures/tinfoilkit/archive/refs/heads/main.zip
    unzip -qo tinfoilkit.zip && rm tinfoilkit.zip
    cd tinfoilkit-main
    ./kit drives --json   # what the kit needs, this computer's free space, and every drive plugged in

On Windows, in PowerShell:

    cd ~
    curl.exe -fL -o tinfoilkit.zip https://github.com/tudor-city-ventures/tinfoilkit/archive/refs/heads/main.zip
    tar -xf tinfoilkit.zip; Remove-Item tinfoilkit.zip
    cd tinfoilkit-main
    python tools\kit.py --root . drives --json

Windows has no `./kit`: run each `./kit COMMAND` in this file as `python tools\kit.py --root . COMMAND`, with Python 3.9 or newer. If `python --version` doesn't print one, ask the person before installing it (`winget install Python.Python.3.13`), or have them double-click SETUP-Windows.bat instead, which gets its own.

It needs no internet and prints needs_gb (the GB the current kit.json needs), needs_essentials_gb (just the essentials), this_computer (path, free_bytes, keeps_free_gb and space) and drives (each with path, format, free_bytes, problem, has_kit, kit_path and space). space says how the kit fits there: full and essentials are each "fits" (leaving 10% of the computer's disk or 5% of a drive free), "tight" (fits, but leaves less) or "no". `./kit space PATH --json` says the same for any folder.

On a Mac without Apple's Command Line Tools, `./kit` stops and says the kit needs Python. Either have the person double-click SETUP.command, which gets a Python for the kit first (about 25 MB) and then walks them through the rest of setup, or, with their OK, install the tools (`xcode-select --install`, several GB, 5 to 15 minutes) and run the command again. `xcode-select -p` shows whether they're there.

Developers can `git clone https://github.com/tudor-city-ventures/tinfoilkit` straight into the chosen place instead, and update with `git pull`.

### 2. Decide where it lives

Go through "Where it can live" with the person, with the numbers from step 1:

- A place fits when its space.full is "fits". "tight" fits too, but leaves less than 10% of the computer's disk (5% of a drive) free: tell the person, and offer just the essentials. "no" doesn't fit: if space.essentials isn't "no", the essentials do (step 3).
- A drive also needs its problem to be null. exFAT works on Mac, Windows and Linux: the best choice for an emergency drive. APFS is fine if the drive will only ever meet Macs.
- A drive with a problem is FAT32 (it can't hold files over 4 GB) or, on a Mac, NTFS (a Mac can't write to it; Windows and Linux can). It needs erasing as exFAT first: on a Mac, in Disk Utility, select the drive, click Erase and choose ExFAT. On Windows, in File Explorer, right-click the drive, choose Format and pick exFAT. Erasing deletes everything on the drive: confirm which disk it is and get the person's explicit yes first.
- A drive with has_kit already holds a kit: offer to update that one instead (see "Update it").

### 3. Choose what goes in it (optional)

kit.json lists everything. The default kit:

- AI models, all of which read photos: Inkling 2 Mini (the default, fast, about 18 GB), Qwen3.8 27B (a second opinion from another lab, slower, 17.5 GB), Gemma 4 26B-A4B (a third opinion, 15.7 GB), Gemma 4 12B (mid-size, for 16 to 24 GB, 7.2 GB) and Gemma 4 E4B (small, saves battery, for 8 GB, 5.3 GB).
- Library: all of English Wikipedia with images (about 115 GB), WikiMed, field and military medicine manuals, LibreTexts textbooks, iFixit repair guides, Ready.gov, US Army publications, Wikibooks, Wiktionary, Wikivoyage, Wikiversity, Appropedia, Energypedia, and Stack Exchange Q&A on home improvement, cooking, gardening, car and bicycle repair, electronics, amateur radio and more. Off by default because they're huge: Survivor Library (232 GB), Khan Academy videos (168 GB) and Project Gutenberg (206 GB).
- Maps: street detail, addresses and directions for one place, address search for that place's whole country, and a low-detail world map. Where nobody publishes address search for the country alone (much of Europe, the Caribbean), it covers the whole region of the world, 16 to 32 GB, and just the essentials (`./kit essentials on`) leave it out. Out of the box the place is the US Northeast (New England, New York, New Jersey, Pennsylvania); set where the person lives (below). 5 to 30 GB, depending on the place.

To change it:

- Skip an item: set "enabled": false on it in models, library or maps.
- Just the essentials: `./kit essentials on` (30 to 50 GB). The kit works with them alone, and `./kit essentials off`, then `./kit sync -y`, gets the rest whenever there's room.
- Skip the models this computer can't run: `./kit fit --skip`.
- Run without the AI: set "enabled": false on every model, or pick No AI in the builder. The library and the map work as usual, Ask shows the best passages instead of an answer, and `./kit test` doesn't ask for a model.
- Add a book: `./kit search WORDS` finds Kiwix books and prints a line to paste into library.
- Where the person lives: ask them, then `./kit region PLACE`, with a US state or a country in English ("Texas", "Ontario", "Germany: Bayern"; nicknames like "UK" and big towns like "Lyon" work too). It sets the map's street detail, directions, address search, home and units, and prints what it set. A big country comes in parts (US states, Canadian provinces, German states): pick the person's part. When a name fits more than one place, it lists them: `./kit region --find WORDS` prints the matches as id, name and group (no words: every place), and `./kit region ID` takes the one meant. `./kit region` alone says what's set now.
- Wikipedia in the person's language: `./kit region --languages PLACE` lists the choices for that place (codes, name, GB). `./kit region PLACE --wikipedia de` (or `de,en` for two) swaps Wikipedia for those, and sync removes the old one once the new one is in.
- Or make a kit.json with the builder at https://tinfoilkit.com/#builder and put it in the kit folder, replacing the one there.

Run `./kit estimate` again after any change.

### 4. Put it in place and fill it

Put the kit where the person chose, with one of:

    KIT="$(./kit place ~/TinfoilKit)" && cd "$KIT"                   # this computer
    KIT="$(./kit place "/Volumes/<drive>/TinfoilKit")" && cd "$KIT"  # a drive: its kit_path from step 1

On Windows: `$KIT = python tools\kit.py --root . place "$HOME\TinfoilKit"` (or `E:\TinfoilKit` for a drive), then `cd $KIT`. Windows can't move a folder a program is using, so there it copies the kit and leaves the download for you to delete.

`./kit place` moves the download there (to another disk it copies the kit, then removes the download), prints the kit's new folder as its only output and sends its messages to stderr. If a kit is already there, it carries on with that one. When it can't, it exits 1 and says why: the drive isn't plugged in, a folder that isn't a kit has the name, or macOS won't let Terminal write to the drive (see "When something goes wrong").

Then, in the kit folder:

    ./kit plan                  # every item, version and size. Show the person the total and get a yes.
    ./kit sync -y --essentials  # the essentials first: the programs, the map, the key books and the AI
    ./kit test                  # start every server offline and check each one answers: now the kit works
    ./kit sync -y               # then everything else: a few hours the first time
    ./kit test

- `./kit sync` exits 0 when everything finished, 1 when something failed or couldn't be looked up, and 130 after Ctrl-C. On 1, run it again: it resumes and names what's left. The kit already works with what it has.
- Sync fetches the most important items first, resumes broken downloads, checks every file against its published checksum when there is one, and deletes an old version only after the new one checks out. Building the directions network takes 10 to 40 minutes after the map downloads.
- If the person has Homebrew, `brew install aria2` makes downloads faster.
- Last, prove it works offline: turn Wi-Fi off, double-click START-HERE.command (START-HERE-Windows.bat on Windows) and ask a question.

### For people who'd rather click

Download https://github.com/tudor-city-ventures/tinfoilkit/archive/refs/heads/main.zip, unzip it and double-click SETUP.command (on Windows, right-click the ZIP, choose Extract All, and double-click SETUP-Windows.bat; on Linux, run `bash SETUP.command`). The first time, it asks where the person lives (a US state or a country, for the maps and Wikipedia's language), then "An external drive" or "This computer", with what fits on each, and moves the kit there. It says which AI the computer runs and asks before downloading models too big for it. Then it downloads and tests the essentials, then the rest, explaining each step. On a Mac without Python, it gets one first. On macOS 15 and later the first double-click says Apple could not verify it: open System Settings > Privacy & Security and click Open Anyway, once. On Windows, if it says Windows protected your PC, click More info, then Run anyway. SETUP asks questions as it goes, so as an agent, run the commands above instead.

## Use it

- Double-click START-HERE.command (START-HERE-Windows.bat on Windows), or run `bash START-HERE.command`. It opens http://127.0.0.1:8888. Keep its window open: closing it stops everything.
- START-HERE.command's options: `--share` lets phones and laptops on the same network open it with an access code (it prints the address, the code and a QR code), `--no-maps` frees about 5 GB of memory, `--model=NAME` picks the first model (a folder name in models/), `--no-browser` skips opening the browser. If macOS asks whether to accept incoming connections, click Allow.
- Ask answers from the books and cites them. AI chat is plain chat that can read a photo but doesn't search the books. Library browses and searches every book. Map searches places, plans routes and finds the nearest hospital, pharmacy or gas station.
- Models: pick one on the Ask page. The first answer after switching takes up to a minute while it loads.
- Map: set home first, since a laptop has no GPS (Set as home on a search result, or Set home to the map center). For actually driving, a phone with offline maps and GPS is better; the kit's map is for planning and for the AI's map questions.
- Power: a big model drains a laptop battery in a couple of hours of steady use. Gemma 4 E4B saves battery, and the Library tab uses almost nothing.
- Linux: Fedora 45 and later need `sudo dnf install openssl3-libs` for the AI, installed while there's still internet.

## A home server

For a computer that stays on, with or without a screen. Set the kit up on the computer's own disk as above (`./kit place ~/TinfoilKit`, `./kit sync -y`, `./kit test`), then, in the kit folder:

    ./kit share on       # share it on the home network behind an access code: prints the address, the code and a QR code
    ./kit autostart on   # start it now, and whenever the computer starts

- `bash SETUP.command --home-server` does the setup and then both. It asks its questions in the terminal, so as an agent, run the commands instead.
- Phones and laptops open the address, like http://192.168.1.20:8000, and type the 8-digit code once; the QR code includes it. `./kit share` shows them again. `./kit share new-code` replaces the code and signs every device out. `./kit share off` stops sharing.
- How it works: tools/share.py listens on the network on port 8000 (`share_port` in kit.json), asks for the code, and passes requests on: /ai/ to the AI, /tiles/, /geocoder/ and /routing/ to the map, everything else to the library. It answers only devices with home network addresses, turns away names that aren't this computer's, and allows 10 wrong codes per 10 minutes from each device.
- Programs can use the code as an API key: `Authorization: Bearer CODE` with the OpenAI-compatible API at http://ADDRESS:8000/ai/v1.
- Linux: autostart is a systemd user service (`systemctl --user status tinfoil-kit`) that starts at boot once lingering is on (`sudo loginctl enable-linger $USER`; the kit tries it and says if it needs you). Mac: a LaunchAgent that starts when the person logs in, so turn on automatic login on a Mac that's a server, and keep the kit on its own disk.
- `./kit autostart off` stops it starting by itself; UNINSTALL does that too. Windows can't share the kit or start it with the computer yet.
- The traffic is plain HTTP inside the home network: share it on the person's own Wi-Fi or hotspot, not a public one.

## Update it

There's no schedule. Whenever the person wants the newest models, books and maps, while online, in the kit folder:

    ./kit update   # the kit's newest version, with any models and sources added since. Keeps the person's kit.json changes.
                   # Installs only a release signed with the kit's key, and asks first at a keyboard (--yes doesn't).
    ./kit plan     # what's new or changed, and how much will download
    ./kit sync -y  # download it, check every file, then remove the old versions
    ./kit test

- `./kit update` exits 3 after installing a newer version of the kit. That's success: carry on with the next command. It exits 0 when the kit is already the newest.
- In a git checkout, run `git pull` instead of `./kit update`.
- An update can bring models too big for this computer: `./kit fit` names them, and `./kit fit --skip` leaves them out. On a kit with just the essentials, `./kit space . --json` says when the rest fits; then run `./kit essentials off` before syncing. SETUP asks about both by itself.
- If `./kit update` says a version isn't signed with the kit's release key, stop: don't install it another way. Tell the person, and report it at https://github.com/tudor-city-ventures/tinfoilkit/security.
- Double-clicking SETUP again (SETUP.command, or SETUP-Windows.bat on Windows) does all four.
- A normal update brings new library editions, the program builds the new kit version names (the AI engine and the rest), any re-released models and fresh map data. Only what changed downloads.
- A book with `refresh_days` in kit.json keeps the edition it has until it's that many days old: Wikipedia (115 GB) has 365, so most updates don't download it again. The plan marks it `later`. `./kit sync --only wikipedia_en_all_maxi` gets the newest now.
- It's safe to stop at any point and run it again: it picks up where it left off, and the old files keep working until the new ones check out.
- `./kit status` shows what's installed and when it was last updated. INVENTORY.md lists every item with its version and size.

## Remove it

Double-click UNINSTALL.command (UNINSTALL-Windows.bat on Windows) in the kit folder. Once the person types "delete", it removes the kit folder and everything the kit downloaded, and the Python SETUP got (on Windows, or on a Mac that had none). On a drive it leaves the rest of the drive alone. As an agent, run `bash UNINSTALL.command --yes` (`.\UNINSTALL-Windows.bat --yes` on Windows), which skips the question, only after the person's explicit yes.

## When something goes wrong

- "Apple could not verify..." on a double-click: System Settings > Privacy & Security > Open Anyway, once. `bash START-HERE.command` in Terminal always works.
- "Windows protected your PC" on a double-click: More info, then Run anyway, once.
- "Operation not permitted" in Terminal: macOS is keeping Terminal off the drive. System Settings > Privacy & Security > Files and Folders > Terminal: turn on Removable Volumes, then start again.
- Sync ended with exit 1, or SETUP says some downloads didn't finish: run `./kit sync -y` again. It resumes and names what's left. The kit already works with what it has.
- Sync says a program's publisher no longer publishes the build the kit names: run `./kit update` first, since a newer kit names newer builds. If it says a program's file changed after the kit pinned it, don't work around it: tell the person, and report it at https://github.com/tudor-city-ventures/tinfoilkit/security.
- Not enough space: sync stops short of the free space it keeps (50 GB on the computer's own disk, 25 GB on a drive). Get just the essentials (`./kit essentials on`), turn items off in kit.json, or move the kit to a bigger drive.
- A file may be corrupt: `./kit verify` re-checks every file. `./kit verify --fix` removes bad ones, and the next sync replaces them.
- A model won't load or is very slow: quit other apps, pick Gemma 4 E4B, or start with `--no-maps` to free about 5 GB. Advanced, with the person's password: `sudo sysctl iogpu.wired_limit_mb=26624` lets the GPU use up to 26 GB until the next restart.
- The map says address search or directions are "not running": they take up to a minute to start. If they never do, read logs/geocoder.log and logs/routing.log. If `./kit test` fails on address search with a "lock" error in logs/test-geocoder.log, the exFAT format is the cause: reformat the drive as APFS and copy the kit back.
- Anything else: close the kit's window, start again, and read the logs folder (sync-*.log for downloads, llama-server.log for the AI).
- The previous version of each program stays in bin/ and starts automatically if the newest one won't.
- If the library server won't start, the Kiwix app in installers/ opens the books in library/ directly.

## Where everything comes from

The kit's own code is MIT. Everything it downloads comes straight from its publisher under the publisher's license: Tinfoil Kit never hosts, mirrors or bundles any of it, and the person is the one downloading, so those terms apply to them. All of it is free to download and use; some of it isn't free to sell. THIRD-PARTY.md has the full list.

- AI models: Inkling 2 Mini by Thinking Machines (Apache 2.0, plus Thinking Machines' Model Acceptable Use Policy, which binds anyone who downloads the weights), Qwen3.8 27B by Alibaba (Apache 2.0), Gemma 4 26B-A4B, Gemma 4 12B and Gemma 4 E4B by Google (Apache 2.0). The files come from ggml-org's and Unsloth's Hugging Face repos.
- Books: Wikipedia and its sister projects, WikiMed, Stack Exchange, Appropedia and Energypedia are CC BY-SA. iFixit, LibreTexts and Khan Academy are CC BY-NC-SA: no commercial use. Ready.gov and US Army publications are US government works. Project Gutenberg is public domain in the US. Survivor Library, Urban Prepper and the collections of field medicine, post-disaster, water, food and knots guides have mixed terms: free to read, not to republish.
- Maps: OpenStreetMap data (© OpenStreetMap contributors, Open Database License), through Protomaps, Geofabrik and the Photon exports GraphHopper hosts. Map style: Protomaps basemaps (BSD-3-Clause). Fonts: Noto Sans (SIL Open Font License).
- Programs: llama.cpp (MIT), kiwix-serve and the Kiwix app (GPL-3.0), Eclipse Temurin Java (GPL-2.0 with Classpath Exception), go-pmtiles (BSD-3-Clause), GraphHopper and Photon (Apache 2.0), MapLibre GL JS (BSD-3-Clause). SETUP also gets Python (PSF License) for the kit's tools on Windows, and on a Mac without one (python-build-standalone's build, which includes OpenSSL, SQLite and other libraries under their own licenses).
- Setup and updates talk only to GitHub, Kiwix, Hugging Face, Protomaps, Geofabrik, GraphHopper, Adoptium, Maven Central and npm, plus nuget.org for Python on Windows and anything added to kit.json. Using the kit sends nothing over the internet: no account, no telemetry.

## Security

- `./kit update` installs new kit code only if the maintainer's release key signed it, checked against tools/release-signers in the copy already there. The key never touches GitHub.
- Every download comes straight from its publisher over HTTPS. Each release names the exact build of every program, with its SHA-256, in tools/pins.json, signed with the rest. Books, models and map data are checked against the publisher's checksum wherever one is posted (the map tiles and fonts have none). Nothing is hosted or mirrored by this project.
- The servers listen on 127.0.0.1. Sharing is off until the person turns it on; then a gate, on port 8000 by default, asks for an 8-digit code. It's plain HTTP, so share on the person's own Wi-Fi or hotspot, not a public network.
- To check a release before running it, download tinfoilkit-TAG.tar.gz and its .sig from the release, then run `ssh-keygen -Y verify -f tools/release-signers -I tinfoilkit-release -n tinfoilkit-release -s tinfoilkit-TAG.tar.gz.sig < tinfoilkit-TAG.tar.gz`.
- Security problems go to https://github.com/tudor-city-ventures/tinfoilkit/security/advisories/new, never a public issue.

## Rules

- Start programs and models only through the kit's own commands. Don't run downloaded files to see what they do.
- Don't delete files in models/, library/ or maps/ by hand. `./kit verify --fix` removes corrupt files, and the next sync replaces them. To remove the whole kit, use UNINSTALL.command.
- Ask before formatting a drive, deleting anything or using sudo.
- Don't sell drives filled with the kit: some sources forbid commercial use.
- The AI can be wrong. For anything medical or safety-related, tell the person to read the sources it cites and to get trained help when they can.
